subject: arcticOutpost
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: arctic research outpost.
Style: Firewatch flat colour.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single static TypeScript scene module for an arctic research outpost diorama, using a flat Firewatch-style warm palette with a snow base, a stilted rust-red cabin, and other supporting structures.

I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and cones to build the diorama parts, then constructing the ice/snow base layers and starting on the cabin's stilts, floor, walls, and gable roof.

Working out the gable roof geometry now—slanted boxes at angled rotations for the roof slabs, triangular gable ends facing front and back, with the ridge running along the depth axis and the slope length calculated from the roof's width and peak height.

Then I plan the front facade: a dark brown door with frame and steps, and glowing warm-yellow windows with cross muntins set into the gable-end wall.

I add side windows, a chimney with soft smoke puffs, and a porch lamp glow, then figure out a tapered radio mast with red/white bands, guy wires, and a blinking red top light, building a small rod helper function for connecting two points with a cylinder. I also start sketching a weather station pole.

Now I'm fleshing out the weather station with anemometer cups, a wind vane, and a louvered Stevenson screen box, plus a satellite dish perched on the shed roof. I shift the shed and surroundings toward a Firewatch-style palette, add striped fuel barrels near the cabin, and start blocking out a snowmobile with a boxy body, windshield, ski, and track.

I'm adding supporting details like a sled with crates, a flag pole, small footprint ovals, icosahedron ice chunks, and background mountains made from low-poly cones with snowcaps arranged along the back edge within the diorama's radius limit. I'm also weighing whether to add a sunset disc behind the mountains, considering a low circle shape partially hidden behind the peaks instead of a floating sun.

I'm now planning snowy pine trees as cone stacks with white caps at the back left, and setting up the base height levels for ice and snow layers before writing the helper functions for placing parts.

Writing builder helper functions...

Now I'm working out the stilted cabin structure—floor height, wall height, and gable roof dimensions built on top of support posts.

Adding siding details like darker vertical trim boards and horizontal siding strips as thin protruding boxes, plus a short front staircase of three steps leading up to the door.

For the chimney, I'm positioning it offset to the side so it rises through the roof surface to just above the ridge, with smoke sphere puffs drifting above it. Time to assemble everything into the final scene, keeping the overall description moderate in length.

Now I'm setting up a window helper that handles both wall orientations, swapping frame/glass/muntin dimensions depending on whether the window faces along x or z, plus a mast with guy wires anchored to the ground in three directions, and a snowmobile built from locally-offset parts rotated into place using a helper that converts local coordinates into world-space boxes.

I'm adding a flagpole near the cabin's front-right corner with a red-orange flag, and arranging mountain cones in a back arc, checking that their radius and placement stay within the scene's base circle so nothing spills past the edge -- adjusting the base radius slightly to keep everything contained.

Now I'm settling on the color palette: warm snow tones, pinkish shadows, icy blue, orange and dark red accents, teal and purple contrasts, and a golden sun glow, before writing out the full scene.
